(LLM note; runs 20261009-175434-0255)
- [note/low_area_control] For area-min CORDIC specs (>=1 MSPS, err <= 2^-10), iterative family with data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=1, rounding=round wins (est 251 luts+ffs, measured 216 LUTs/107 FFs/150.7 MHz). Cost model underestimates LUTs by ~19% and FFs by ~11% vs yosys+nextpnr-xilinx; Fmax underestimated by ~10%. Pipelined variants too area-hungry for this class. (LLM note; runs 20261009-175238-0eca)

    spec dds_250msps: NCO / DDS sin-cos generator for a digital up-converter. One sample per clock at >= 250 MSPS, max error <= 2^-13. Minimise LUTs.
      constraint: throughput_msps >= 250
      constraint: max_abs_err <= 0.00012207
      objective: min luts (HV ref 4000)
      objective: max accuracy_bits (HV ref 13)
      select: min luts
      budget: 400 evals, 100/round, <= 4 rounds, eps 0.01

args.notes: DDS spec: 1 sample/clock at >=250 MSPS, err <= 2^-13, min LUTs. Pipelined_m (m=1) is the natural family for 1-sample-per-clock; iterative is too slow (12 cycles/sample ~ 83 MSPS at 1GHz). unrolled_k likely area-hungry. Prior calibration: cost model underestimates LUTs ~19%, FFs ~11%, Fmax ~10% vs yosys+nextpnr-xilinx. Favor data_width ~16-18, n_iter ~14-16 for 2^-13 accuracy.

args.lesson: For high-rate (>=250 MSPS, 1 sample/clock) CORDIC specs with err <= 2^-13, min LUTs: pipelined (m=1) family with data_width=18, n_iter=15, angle_guard=2, frac_guard=0, rounding=round wins (est 920 LUTs, 953 FFs, 264 MSPS, err 2^-13.17). The sweet spot is data_width 18, n_iter 15; angle_guard 2 with rounding=round is cheapest. No L3/L4 measurements recorded for this design; L5 back_annotate returned no_measured_data.
